said: At 10x a feature has to subtend about 3.5 arcminutes to be centered on, so at 100 yd the white center is 0.37 in across.

The bull is a black disc 1.11 in across with that white center and a small dot in the middle: the aim is the white center, which a crosshair cannot cover, as it covered the thin cross and the open gap in the aim point test.
25 bulls on one letter sheet, 1.51 in apart: one shot per bull.
At 4x a feature has to subtend about 3.5 arcminutes to be centered on, so at 100 yd the white center is 0.92 in across.

The bull is a black disc 2.74 in across with that white center and a small dot in the middle: the aim is the white center, which a crosshair cannot cover, as it covered the thin cross and the open gap in the aim point test.
4 bulls a sheet, 3.70 in apart, on 7 sheets: one shot per bull. Each sheet's codes say which of the 7 it is.
That is 28 bulls for 25 shots; leave 3 empty and enter the rounds fired, so GroupLab expects 25.
